speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to your consultation. I need to examine any skin lesions you are concerned about, particularly those with potential oncologic implications. Can you describe the location, size, shape, and color of the most suspicious spot you've noticed?

speaker: Patient
text: 62-year-old male. The patient has recently immigrated to the US from Africa and seeks evaluation for a non-healing, red, crusty lesion on the shaft of his penis and a similar lesion on his left middle finger. Previous treatments in his home country for syphilis and eczema have been unsuccessful. The patient is a smoker, with a history of two packs per day for the last 30 years.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Squamous Cell Carcinoma of the Penis and Finger (Multicentric SCC). The patient's age, heavy smoking history, African origin, and non-healing, crusted lesions on the penis and finger despite prior treatments for syphilis/eczema are highly suggestive of invasive squamous cell carcinoma, with the finger lesion likely representing a squamous cell carcinoma arising in a chronic skin lesion (such as a callus or chronic ulcer) or possibly a separate primary. Immediate biopsy of both lesions is required for confirmation and staging.

REQUEST TEST: Biopsy_Penile_Lesion, Biopsy_Finger_Lesion, Complete_Blood_Count, Liver_Function_Tests, Chest_XRay, PSA
REQUEST IMAGES: Dermoscopy_Penile_Lesion, Dermoscopy_Finger_Lesion
